board_events.caption: The same pair wired both ways: in series the higher-resistance bulb wins, in parallel the higher-wattage bulb wins.

board_events.text: In series the current is common, so brightness follows $P = I^2R$ and the higher resistance glows brighter.
Since the forty watt bulb has the higher resistance, it is the forty watt bulb that glows brighter in series.
Memory hook: in series the weaker bulb wins; in parallel the stronger bulb wins.

segments.text: The second worked example is the classic N E E T speed trap of this subtopic, and almost everyone gets it wrong the first time.
Two bulbs, rated one hundred watt and forty watt, both at two hundred forty volt, are connected in series across a two hundred forty volt supply. Which one glows brighter?
<chuckle>The instinct is immediate and wrong.</chuckle> The hundred watt bulb is the more powerful one, so surely it must be brighter. In series it is not.
Look at the two wirings side by side, because the answer genuinely flips between them. Series and parallel give opposite winners for the same pair of bulbs.
Work out the resistances first, from the ratings. The hundred watt bulb comes out at five hundred seventy six ohm, and the forty watt bulb at one thousand four hundred forty ohm.
Now apply the rule we built. In series the current is common to both, so brightness follows current squared times resistance, and the higher resistance dissipates more.
Since the lower-wattage bulb has the higher resistance, it is the forty watt bulb that glows brighter in series.
The memory hook is worth keeping: in series the weaker bulb wins, and in parallel the stronger bulb wins. One line covers both halves of every question of this type.
Doosra worked example इस subtopic का classic N E E T speed trap है, और लगभग हर कोई पहली बार में ग़लत करता है।
Do bulbs, एक सौ watt और चालीस watt के, दोनों दो सौ चालीस volt के लिए rated, दो सौ चालीस volt की supply के आर पार series में जुड़े हैं। कौन सा तेज़ जलेगा?
Pehla ख़याल तुरंत आता है और ग़लत होता है। सौ watt वाला ज़्यादा ताक़तवर है, तो ज़ाहिर है वही तेज़ होगा। Series में ऐसा नहीं है।
<curious>Dono wirings साथ साथ देखिए</curious>, क्योंकि answer इनके बीच सचमुच पलट जाता है। एक ही जोड़ी के लिए series और parallel उल्टे विजेता देते हैं।
Pehle ratings से resistances निकालिए। सौ watt वाला निकलता है पाँच सौ छिहत्तर ohm, और चालीस watt वाला एक हज़ार चार सौ चालीस ohm।
Ab वो नियम लगाइए जो हमने बनाया था। Series में current दोनों में एक ही है, इसलिए brightness current squared into resistance के हिसाब से चलती है, और ज़्यादा resistance ज़्यादा खपाती है।
Kyunki कम wattage वाले bulb की resistance ज़्यादा है, series में चालीस watt वाला bulb ही तेज़ जलता है।
Yaad रखने वाला हुक क़ीमती है: series में कमज़ोर bulb जीतता है, और parallel में ताक़तवर bulb। एक line इस तरह के हर सवाल के दोनों हिस्से सँभाल लेती है।

sections.title: Worked example: monthly energy and the bill

board_events.text: Worked example, J E E Main level: energy and the electricity bill
A household runs a one point five kilowatt water geyser for two hours every day, for thirty days.
Electricity costs eight rupees per kilowatt hour. Find the monthly energy consumed and its cost.
Work directly in kilowatt hours: power in kilowatt multiplied by time in hours gives energy in kilowatt hour.
So the geyser accounts for ninety units and seven hundred twenty rupees on the monthly bill.
In joules that same energy is $3.24\times10^{8}$, which is exactly why the kilowatt hour exists as a billing unit.

segments.text: The third worked example is at J E E Main level, though the arithmetic is everyday. It is really a lesson in choosing units.
A household runs a one point five kilowatt water geyser for two hours every day, for thirty days.
Electricity costs eight rupees per kilowatt hour, and you are asked for the monthly energy consumed and the cost of it.

<whisper>Here is the whole technique.</whisper> Work directly in kilowatt hours from start to finish. Power in kilowatt multiplied by time in hours gives energy in kilowatt hour, with no conversion needed anywhere.
The total running time is two hours a day for thirty days, which is sixty hours. Multiply by one point five kilowatt and you get ninety kilowatt hours.
Ninety units at eight rupees a unit gives seven hundred twenty rupees.
So the geyser alone accounts for ninety units and seven hundred twenty rupees on the monthly bill, which is the kind of answer you can sanity check against real life.

For contrast, that same energy in joules is three point two four times ten to the eight. Notice how clumsy that is to work with and to quote, which is exactly why the kilowatt hour exists as a billing unit at all.
Teesra worked example J E E Main level का है, हालाँकि arithmetic रोज़मर्रा की है। ये असल में units चुनने का सबक़ है।
Ek घर में एक point पाँच kilowatt का water geyser रोज़ दो घंटे चलता है, तीस दिन तक।
Bijli की क़ीमत आठ रुपये per kilowatt hour है, और आपसे महीने की खपी हुई energy और उसकी लागत पूछी गई है।
Ye रही पूरी तकनीक। शुरू से आख़िर तक सीधे kilowatt hour में काम कीजिए। Power kilowatt में into time घंटों में देता है energy kilowatt hour में, और कहीं कोई conversion नहीं चाहिए।
Kul चलने का समय है रोज़ दो घंटे, तीस दिन, यानी साठ घंटे। एक point पाँच kilowatt से गुणा कीजिए और नब्बे kilowatt hour मिलते हैं।
<curious>Nabbe units, आठ रुपये per unit</curious>, देते हैं सात सौ बीस रुपये।
To अकेला geyser महीने के bill में नब्बे units और सात सौ बीस रुपये का हिसाब बनाता है, और ये वैसा answer है जिसे आप असली ज़िंदगी से मिलाकर जाँच सकते हैं।
Tulna के लिए, वही energy joule में है three point two four into ten to the eight। देखिए उसके साथ काम करना और उसे बोलना कितना भारी है, और ठीक इसीलिए kilowatt hour नाम की billing unit मौजूद है।

sections.title: Worked example: maximum power transfer with numbers

board_events.text: Worked example, J E E Advanced: matching the load
A battery of electromotive force twelve volt has internal resistance two ohm. A variable resistor $R$ is connected as the load.
Find the value of $R$ for maximum power transfer, the maximum power delivered, and the efficiency at that point.
The other eighteen watt is wasted inside the battery. Maximum power transfer is a fifty percent efficient compromise.

segments.text: The final worked example is at J E E Advanced level, and it puts real numbers on the maximum power transfer theorem.
A battery of electromotive force twelve volt has internal resistance two ohm, and a variable resistor is connected across it as the load.
You are asked for three things: the load value for maximum power transfer, the maximum power delivered, and the efficiency at that operating point.
The first part needs no calculation at all. Maximum power transfer occurs when the load matches the internal resistance, so the answer is two ohm.
For the maximum power, substitute into the result we derived. Twelve squared is one hundred forty four, divided by four times two, which is eight, giving eighteen watt.

For the efficiency, find the current at the match point. Twelve volt across a total of four ohm gives three amperes, so the total power drawn from the battery is twelve times three, which is thirty six watt.
The load receives eighteen of those thirty six watt, so the efficiency is exactly fifty percent, confirming the general result.

<curious>Where does the rest go?</curious> The other eighteen watt is wasted inside the battery itself, heating its own internal resistance. Maximum power transfer is a fifty percent efficient compromise, useful for signal matching and never for power distribution.
Aakhri worked example J E E Advanced level का है, और ये maximum power transfer theorem पर असली numbers रखता है।
Ek battery जिसका electromotive force बारह volt है और internal resistance दो ohm, उसके आर पार load की तरह एक बदलने वाला resistor जुड़ा है।
Aapse तीन चीज़ें पूछी गई हैं: maximum power transfer के लिए load की value, दी गई अधिकतम power, और उस operating point पर efficiency।
<curious>Pehle हिस्से में कोई calculation है ही नहीं।</curious> Maximum power transfer तब होता है जब load internal resistance से मेल खाए, इसलिए answer है दो ohm।
Adhiktam power के लिए उस नतीजे में रखिए जो हमने derive किया था। बारह का square है एक सौ चवालीस, चार into दो यानी आठ से divide, जिससे अठारह watt मिलता है।
Efficiency के लिए मेल वाले point पर current निकालिए। कुल चार ohm पर बारह volt देता है तीन ampere, इसलिए battery से ली गई कुल power है बारह into तीन, यानी छत्तीस watt।
Load को उन छत्तीस में से अठारह watt मिलते हैं, इसलिए efficiency ठीक पचास percent है, जो आम नतीजे की पुष्टि करता है।

Baaki कहाँ जाता है? बाक़ी अठारह watt battery के अंदर ही बर्बाद होता है, उसकी अपनी internal resistance को गरम करते हुए। Maximum power transfer पचास percent efficient समझौता है, signal matching के लिए काम का और power distribution के लिए कभी नहीं।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for energy and power

board_events.text: Pitfalls that cost marks, and the pro-tips that save time
Using the wrong power formula for the situation. Picking the wrong face flips your brightness answer entirely.
Treating a bulb's rated resistance as fixed at all voltages. The cold filament has far lower resistance than the rated value.
Forgetting the square in the voltage relation. Halving the voltage quarters the power, it does not halve it.
Confusing maximum power with maximum efficiency. They occur at completely different conditions.
Ask first what is shared, current or voltage, and the right formula picks itself instantly.
For billing, keep power in kilowatt and time in hours from start to finish, and never convert to joule unless the question asks.

segments.text: Let us close this subtopic with the four errors that cost marks and the two habits that prevent nearly all of them.

The first is using the wrong power formula for the situation. All three forms are algebraically true, so this is not about being wrong, it is about being useless. Picking the wrong face flips your brightness answer entirely.

The second is treating a bulb's rated resistance as fixed at every voltage. Sixty watt at two hundred forty volt gives you the resistance at two hundred forty volt, and the cold filament has far lower resistance than that.
The third is forgetting the square in the voltage relation. With resistance fixed, power goes as voltage squared, so halving the voltage quarters the power rather than halving it.

The fourth is confusing maximum power with maximum efficiency. They occur at completely different conditions, and the option claiming full efficiency at the match point is the most common trap in multiple choice questions.

<excited>Now the two habits.</excited> For any brightness or dissipation comparison, ask first what is shared. Series shares the current, so use current squared times resistance. Parallel shares the voltage, so use voltage squared over resistance.
That single question picks the right formula instantly, and it removes the guesswork that produces most wrong answers here.
And for any billing question, keep power in kilowatt and time in hours from start to finish. Never convert to joule unless the question explicitly asks for joule.
Is subtopic को उन चार ग़लतियों के साथ ख़त्म करते हैं जो marks काटती हैं, और उन दो आदतों के साथ जो लगभग सब रोक देती हैं।

<curious>Pehli है हालत के हिसाब से ग़लत power formula इस्तेमाल करना।</curious> तीनों रूप algebraically सही हैं, इसलिए बात ग़लत होने की नहीं, बेकार होने की है। ग़लत चेहरा चुनने से brightness का answer पूरी तरह पलट जाता है।
Doosri है bulb की rated resistance को हर voltage पर स्थिर मान लेना। दो सौ चालीस volt पर साठ watt आपको दो सौ चालीस volt पर की resistance देता है, और ठंडे filament की resistance उससे कहीं कम होती है।
Teesri है voltage वाले relation में square भूल जाना। Resistance स्थिर हो तो power voltage के square के हिसाब से चलती है, इसलिए voltage आधा करने पर power आधी नहीं, एक चौथाई होती है।
Chauthi है maximum power को maximum efficiency समझ लेना। ये बिलकुल अलग हालतों पर होते हैं, और मेल वाले point पर पूरी efficiency का दावा करने वाला option multiple choice में सबसे आम जाल है।

Ab दो आदतें। किसी भी brightness या खपत की तुलना में पहले पूछिए कि साझा क्या है। Series current साझा करता है, तो current squared into resistance इस्तेमाल कीजिए। Parallel voltage साझा करता है, तो voltage squared over resistance।
Wo एक सवाल सही formula तुरंत चुन देता है, और वो अंदाज़ेबाज़ी हटा देता है जो यहाँ ज़्यादातर ग़लत answers पैदा करती है।
Aur किसी भी billing सवाल में power को kilowatt और time को घंटों में शुरू से आख़िर तक रखिए। Joule में तब तक मत जाइए जब तक सवाल साफ़ साफ़ joule न माँगे।

sections.title: A cell is a charge pump, and EMF is not a force

board_events.text: A cell is a charge pump
Chemical reactions inside a cell do work to lift positive charge from the low-potential terminal to the high-potential terminal.
They lift it against the electric field, exactly as a water pump lifts water uphill against gravity.
The electromotive force is the energy this pump gives to each coulomb of charge that passes through it.
Despite its name, electromotive force is not a force. Its unit is the volt, which is energy per unit charge.
Its dimensional formula is $M L^{2} T^{-3} A^{-1}$, identical to potential difference, and nothing like the dimensions of a force.
Calling it a force costs an easy definition mark in board exams every year.

segments.text: We now open up the battery itself, which we have treated as an ideal source for four subtopics and which is about to stop being ideal.
Chemical reactions inside a cell do work to lift positive charge from the low-potential terminal to the high-potential terminal.
Notice the direction. They lift charge against the electric field, exactly as a water pump lifts water uphill against gravity. Left alone, the charge would flow the other way.
The quantity that measures this pumping is the electromotive force, defined as the work done by the source per unit charge that passes through it.
In words, it is the energy the pump gives to each coulomb, and it is the full pressure the cell can offer when nothing at all is being drawn from it.
<whisper>Now the definition trap.</whisper> Despite its name, electromotive force is not a force. Its unit is the volt, which is energy per unit charge.
You can settle it with dimensions. Its dimensional formula is M, L squared, T to the minus three, A to the minus one, identical to potential difference and nothing like the dimensions of a force.
Calling it a force costs an easy definition mark in board exams every single year, and it is entirely avoidable once you have said the word volt out loud.
Ab हम battery को ख़ुद खोलते हैं, जिसे हमने चार subtopics तक ideal source माना है और जो अब ideal होना बंद करने वाली है।
Cell के अंदर chemical reactions काम करके positive charge को कम potential वाले terminal से ज़्यादा potential वाले terminal तक उठाते हैं।
<curious>Disha पर ध्यान दीजिए।</curious> वो charge को electric field के ख़िलाफ़ उठाते हैं, बिलकुल जैसे पानी का pump गुरुत्व के ख़िलाफ़ पानी ऊपर चढ़ाता है। छोड़ दें तो charge उल्टी तरफ़ बहेगा।
Jo चीज़ इस pumping को मापती है वो है electromotive force, जिसे source द्वारा per unit charge किए गए काम के रूप में define करते हैं।
Shabdon में, ये वो energy है जो pump हर coulomb को देता है, और यही वो पूरा दबाव है जो cell दे सकता है जब उससे कुछ भी न खींचा जा रहा हो।
Ab definition वाला जाल। नाम के बावजूद, electromotive force कोई force है ही नहीं। इसका unit volt है, यानी energy per unit charge।
Ise dimensions से तय कर लीजिए। इसका dimensional formula है M, L squared, T to the minus three, A to the minus one, बिलकुल potential difference जैसा और force के dimensions से बिलकुल अलग।
Ise force कह देना हर साल board exams में एक आसान definition का mark ले जाता है, और एक बार volt शब्द ज़ोर से बोल लेने के बाद ये पूरी तरह बचाया जा सकता है।

sections.title: Internal resistance and why terminal voltage sags

board_events.text: Why the terminal voltage sags
No real pump is perfect. The chemicals and electrodes inside the cell themselves resist the flow of charge.
That opposition is the internal resistance $r$, and it is in series with the ideal source inside the cell.

board_events.caption: Terminal voltage against current: a straight line with intercept E and slope minus r, from open circuit down to short circuit.

board_events.text: With the cell idle and no current flowing, you measure its full electromotive force across the terminals.
The instant you connect a load and current flows, $Ir$ volts are lost inside the cell itself.
Picture a roof tank with a tap downstairs: shut the tap and you read full pressure, open it wide and the pressure at the tap sags.

segments.text: Now we add the one piece of realism that changes every circuit calculation from here onwards.
No real pump is perfect. The chemicals and the electrodes inside the cell themselves resist the flow of charge through the cell.
That opposition is called the internal resistance, written r, and we model it as an ordinary resistor sitting in series with an ideal source inside the cell.
The consequence shows up beautifully on a graph of terminal voltage against current. It is a straight line, and both quantities you care about are readable from it.
Start at the left end. With the cell idle and no current flowing, you measure its full electromotive force across the terminals, which is the intercept of the line.
<curious>Now connect a load.</curious> The instant current flows, some of the cell's push is spent overcoming its own internal resistance, and I r volts are lost inside the cell itself.
What is left for the outside world is the terminal voltage, which is therefore the electromotive force minus that internal drop. The slope of the line is minus r.

The picture to hold is a water tank on the roof with a tap downstairs. Shut the tap and you read the full pressure. Open it wide and the pressure at the tap sags, because the narrow internal pipe eats some of it.
Ab हम वो एक हक़ीक़त जोड़ते हैं जो यहाँ से आगे हर circuit की गणना बदल देती है।
Koi असली pump परिपूर्ण नहीं होता। Cell के अंदर के chemicals और electrodes ख़ुद cell में charge के बहने का विरोध करते हैं।
<curious>Us विरोध को internal resistance कहते हैं</curious>, जिसे r लिखते हैं, और हम इसे cell के अंदर एक ideal source के series में बैठे साधारण resistor की तरह मानते हैं।
Iska नतीजा terminal voltage versus current के graph पर बहुत ख़ूबसूरती से दिखता है। वो एक सीधी line है, और जिन दोनों चीज़ों की आपको फ़िक्र है वो उसी से पढ़ी जा सकती हैं।
Baayen सिरे से शुरू कीजिए। Cell खाली बैठा हो और कोई current न बह रहा हो, तो terminals पर आप उसका पूरा electromotive force मापते हैं, जो line का intercept है।
Ab एक load जोड़िए। जिस पल current बहता है, cell का कुछ धक्का उसकी अपनी internal resistance पार करने में लग जाता है, और I r volt cell के अंदर ही खो जाते हैं।
Bahar की दुनिया के लिए जो बचता है वो terminal voltage है, यानी electromotive force minus वो अंदरूनी drop। Line का slope minus r है।
Yaad रखने वाली तस्वीर है छत पर रखा पानी का tank जिसका tap नीचे है। Tap बंद कीजिए और आप पूरा दबाव पढ़ते हैं। पूरा खोलिए और tap पर दबाव गिर जाता है, क्योंकि पतली अंदरूनी pipe कुछ खा जाती है।

sections.title: Short circuit, charging, and the limits of the model

board_events.text: Short circuit, charging, and the limits of the model
Open the tap fully with no resistance outside at all, and the flow is limited only by the internal pipe.
The short-circuit current is large but strictly finite, capped by the internal resistance. It never runs away to infinity.
There is also the reverse situation. When you charge a battery, you force current into it against its own electromotive force.
So the terminal voltage of a charging battery is greater than its electromotive force, which is how you recognise the charging case.
The model treats the cell as an ideal source with a fixed $r$, but in reality $r$ drifts with temperature, with age, and with state of charge.

segments.text: Two extreme cases finish the physical picture, and both are exam favourites in their own right.
Take the tank analogy to its limit. Open the tap fully with no resistance outside at all, and the flow is limited only by the narrow internal pipe.
That is the short circuit. With zero external resistance, the current is simply the electromotive force divided by the internal resistance.

<whisper>Note carefully what this does not say.</whisper> The short-circuit current is large, and dangerously so for a real cell, but it is strictly finite. The internal resistance caps it, and it never runs away to infinity.
There is also the reverse situation, which students meet less often and handle worse. When you charge a battery, you force current into it against its own electromotive force.
Now the external source must overcome both the cell's electromotive force and its internal drop, so the two terms add instead of subtracting.

The consequence is worth memorising as a recognition test. The terminal voltage of a charging battery is greater than its electromotive force, and spotting that tells you immediately which sign to use.

One honest caveat about the model. We treat the cell as an ideal source with a fixed internal resistance, but in reality that resistance drifts with temperature, with age, and with how far the cell has run down.
Do चरम मामले इस physical तस्वीर को पूरा करते हैं, और दोनों अपने आप में exam के पसंदीदा हैं।
Tank वाली analogy को उसके सिरे तक ले जाइए। Tap पूरा खोल दीजिए और बाहर कोई resistance ही न हो, तो बहाव सिर्फ़ पतली अंदरूनी pipe से ही सीमित होगा।
Wahi short circuit है। External resistance zero हो तो current बस electromotive force divided by internal resistance है।

Dhyan से देखिए ये क्या नहीं कह रहा। Short-circuit current बड़ा होता है, और असली cell के लिए ख़तरनाक हद तक, लेकिन वो बिलकुल finite है। Internal resistance उसे बाँध देती है, और वो कभी infinity तक नहीं भागता।

<curious>Ek उल्टा मामला भी है</curious>, जो students को कम मिलता है और वो उसे ज़्यादा ख़राब सँभालते हैं। Battery charge करते समय आप current को उसके अपने electromotive force के ख़िलाफ़ अंदर धकेलते हैं।
Ab external source को cell का अपना electromotive force और उसका अंदरूनी drop दोनों पार करने पड़ते हैं, इसलिए दोनों terms घटने की जगह जुड़ते हैं।
Iska नतीजा पहचान की जाँच की तरह याद रखने लायक़ है। Charge होती battery का terminal voltage उसके electromotive force से ज़्यादा होता है, और यही देख लेना तुरंत बता देता है कि कौन सा sign लगेगा।
Model के बारे में एक ईमानदार बात। हम cell को तय internal resistance वाला ideal source मानते हैं, लेकिन असल में वो resistance temperature, उम्र, और cell कितना ख़ाली हो चुका है, इन सबसे खिसकती रहती है।

sections.title: EMF, terminal voltage and the load current

board_events.text: EMF, terminal voltage and the load current
SI unit: the volt, one joule per coulomb, dimensional formula $M L^{2} T^{-3} A^{-1}$.

board_events.latex: V = E - Ir \quad \text{(discharging)}, \qquad V = E + Ir \quad \text{(charging)}

board_events.text: Subtract while the cell supplies current; add while an external source forces current into it.
For a single cell driving an external load, the current is the electromotive force divided by the total resistance of the loop.
The terminal voltage is then simply the drop across the external resistor, which gives a free cross-check on every answer.

segments.text: Here is the first formula block, and the sign convention in the second line carries more marks than anything else in this subtopic.
Electromotive force is defined as the work done by the source per unit charge passing through it.
Its S I unit is the volt, which is one joule per coulomb, with dimensional formula M, L squared, T to the minus three, A to the minus one.
The terminal voltage relation carries two signs, and they are not interchangeable.
Subtract the internal drop while the cell is supplying current, and add it while an external source is forcing current into the cell. Discharging subtracts, charging adds.
For a single cell driving an external load, apply the loop rule and the current is the electromotive force divided by the total resistance of the loop, meaning external plus internal.

<curious>Read the second expression carefully.</curious> The terminal voltage is simply the drop across the external resistor, because those two terminals are exactly where the external resistor is connected.
That gives you a free cross-check on every answer in this subtopic. Compute the terminal voltage both ways, as E minus I r and as I R, and the two must agree.
Ye पहला formula हिस्सा है, और दूसरी line का sign convention इस subtopic में किसी भी और चीज़ से ज़्यादा marks ले जाता है।
Electromotive force को source द्वारा उससे गुज़रते per unit charge किए गए काम के रूप में define करते हैं।
Iska S I unit volt है, यानी एक joule per coulomb, dimensional formula M, L squared, T to the minus three, A to the minus one के साथ।
Terminal voltage वाले relation में दो sign हैं, और वो आपस में बदले नहीं जा सकते।
<curious>Jab cell current दे रहा हो तो अंदरूनी drop घटाइए</curious>, और जब कोई external source cell में current धकेल रहा हो तो जोड़िए। Discharging घटाता है, charging जोड़ता है।
Ek अकेले cell के लिए जो external load चला रहा है, loop rule लगाइए और current मिलता है electromotive force divided by loop की कुल resistance, यानी external plus internal।
Doosri expression ध्यान से पढ़िए। Terminal voltage बस external resistor पर का drop है, क्योंकि वो दोनों terminals ठीक वहीं हैं जहाँ external resistor जुड़ा है।
Isse आपको इस subtopic के हर answer पर एक मुफ़्त cross-check मिल जाता है। Terminal voltage दोनों तरीक़ों से निकालिए, E minus I r से और I R से, और दोनों को मिलना ही चाहिए।

sections.title: Internal resistance from measurement, and special cases

board_events.text: Internal resistance from a measurement, and the special cases
In words: the voltage you lost, divided by the current you drew. This is the cleanest route from data.
These two forms are useful when you know the external resistance rather than the current directly.
Open circuit means zero current, so the terminal voltage equals the electromotive force exactly.
Short circuit means zero external resistance, so the current is $E/r$ and the terminal voltage collapses to zero.
The load power carries the same form we met in the previous subtopic, which is why maximum power transfer belongs to both.

segments.text: The second formula block gives you every route from measured data to the internal resistance, plus the two limiting cases.
The cleanest route is the first one: the internal resistance equals the electromotive force minus the terminal voltage, all divided by the current.
Say it in words and you will never misremember it. The voltage you lost, divided by the current you drew. That phrasing alone solves most numerical questions here.
Two further forms appear when you are given the external resistance instead of the current, and both follow by substituting the current as V over R.
These are useful in exactly the situation where a voltmeter reading and a known load resistance are supplied, which is the standard laboratory setup.
<curious>Now the two limiting cases.</curious> Open circuit means zero current, so no internal drop occurs at all and the terminal voltage equals the electromotive force exactly.
Short circuit means zero external resistance, so the current becomes E over r and the terminal voltage collapses to zero. Those two cases sit at the two ends of the straight line we drew earlier.
Finally, the power delivered to the load carries exactly the same form we met in the energy and power subtopic.
That shared form is why maximum power transfer genuinely belongs to both topics, and why a question can arrive from either direction.
Doosra formula हिस्सा मापे गए data से internal resistance तक का हर रास्ता देता है, और साथ में दोनों सीमावर्ती मामले।
Sabse साफ़ रास्ता पहला है: internal resistance बराबर electromotive force minus terminal voltage, पूरा current से divide।
Ise शब्दों में कहिए और आप इसे कभी ग़लत याद नहीं करेंगे। जो voltage खोया, उसे उस current से divide कीजिए जो खींचा। अकेला यही वाक्य यहाँ के ज़्यादातर सवाल हल कर देता है।
<curious>Do और रूप तब आते हैं</curious> जब आपको current की जगह external resistance दी गई हो, और दोनों current को V over R रखने से निकल आते हैं।
Ye ठीक उसी हालत में काम आते हैं जहाँ voltmeter की reading और एक known load resistance दी गई हो, जो standard laboratory setup है।
Ab दोनों सीमावर्ती मामले। Open circuit का मतलब zero current, इसलिए कोई अंदरूनी drop होता ही नहीं और terminal voltage बिलकुल electromotive force के बराबर होता है।

Short circuit का मतलब zero external resistance, इसलिए current बन जाता है E over r और terminal voltage गिरकर zero हो जाता है। ये दोनों मामले उसी सीधी line के दोनों सिरों पर बैठे हैं जो हमने पहले खींची थी।
Aakhir में, load को मिलने वाली power का रूप बिलकुल वही है जो energy और power वाले subtopic में मिला था।
Wahi साझा रूप वजह है कि maximum power transfer सचमुच दोनों topics का है, और सवाल किसी भी तरफ़ से आ सकता है।

board_events.text: Draw the cell as a dashed box containing an ideal source and $r$ in series. The terminals sit on the outside of that box.
Apply the loop rule around the circuit. The electromotive force supplies $E$ per coulomb, and it is spent on two drops.
Physical reading: the terminal voltage is the full electromotive force minus the voltage lost inside the cell.

segments.text: This is the derivation C B S E asks for by name, and it is four lines once the diagram is drawn correctly.
Take a cell of electromotive force E and internal resistance r, connected to an external resistor R, driving a steady current I around the loop.
The drawing is doing real work here. Show the cell as a dashed box containing an ideal source in series with the internal resistance, with the two terminals sitting on the outside of that box.
That layout makes the whole result visible before you write anything, because you can see the internal resistance is inside the box and the terminal voltage is measured outside it.
Now apply the loop rule around the circuit, which is just energy conservation for one lap. The electromotive force supplies E per coulomb, and that energy is spent on exactly two drops.
Those two drops are the internal one, I r, and the external one, I R, so the electromotive force equals their sum.
The terminal voltage is the potential difference across the cell's terminals, which equals the drop across the external resistor. Substituting I R from the loop equation gives V equals E minus I r.

<curious>Read the result physically.</curious> The terminal voltage is the full electromotive force minus the voltage lost inside the cell. When the current is zero no internal drop occurs, which is why an open-circuit voltmeter reads the electromotive force.
Ye वो derivation है जिसे C B S E नाम लेकर पूछता है, और diagram ठीक बन जाने के बाद ये चार lines की है।
Ek cell लीजिए जिसका electromotive force E और internal resistance r है, जो external resistor R से जुड़ा है और loop में steady current I चला रहा है।
Yahan drawing असली काम कर रही है। Cell को एक dashed box की तरह दिखाइए जिसमें एक ideal source internal resistance के series में है, और दोनों terminals उस box के बाहर बैठे हैं।
<curious>Wo layout पूरा नतीजा कुछ लिखने से पहले ही दिखा देता है</curious>, क्योंकि आप देख सकते हैं कि internal resistance box के अंदर है और terminal voltage उसके बाहर मापा जा रहा है।
Ab circuit के चारों तरफ़ loop rule लगाइए, जो एक चक्कर के लिए बस energy conservation है। Electromotive force per coulomb E देता है, और वो energy ठीक दो drops में ख़र्च होती है।
Wo दो drops हैं अंदरूनी I r, और बाहरी I R, इसलिए electromotive force उनके जोड़ के बराबर है।
Terminal voltage cell के terminals के बीच का potential difference है, जो external resistor पर के drop के बराबर है। Loop equation से I R रखने पर मिलता है V equals E minus I r।

Natije को physically पढ़िए। Terminal voltage पूरा electromotive force minus cell के अंदर खोया हुआ voltage है। Current zero हो तो कोई अंदरूनी drop होता ही नहीं, और इसीलिए open-circuit voltmeter electromotive force पढ़ता है।

board_events.text: The external source must now overcome both the cell's electromotive force and its internal drop, so both add.
Now the standard laboratory procedure for finding both $E$ and $r$ when neither is known.

board_events.latex: E = I_1(R_1 + r), \qquad E = I_2(R_2 + r)

board_events.text: One measurement gives one equation in two unknowns. A second independent measurement closes the system, and equating the two eliminates $E$.

segments.text: This section covers the charging sign and then the two-load procedure, which is both a standard lab method and a J E E staple.
When an external source pushes current into the cell, the current flows opposite to the cell's normal discharge direction.
Draw it and the reversal is obvious: the supply is on one side, a series resistor limits the current, and the battery sits on the other side being driven backwards.

Now the sign flips, and it is worth stating why rather than memorising it. The external source must overcome both the cell's own electromotive force and its internal drop, so both terms add to the required terminal voltage.
That gives terminal voltage equals E plus I r, and the terminal voltage of a charging battery is therefore greater than its electromotive force.
<curious>Now the procedure for finding both unknowns.</curious> Connect the cell to a known resistance and measure the current, then repeat with a different known resistance.
Each measurement gives you the electromotive force as the current times the total loop resistance, so you have two equations of exactly the same shape.

One measurement alone gives one equation in two unknowns and cannot be solved. The second independent measurement closes the system, and equating the two expressions eliminates the electromotive force so the internal resistance falls out in a single step.
Ye section charging वाला sign और फिर two-load procedure बताता है, जो एक standard lab method भी है और J E E का पक्का सवाल भी।
Jab कोई external source cell में current धकेलता है, तो current cell की सामान्य discharge दिशा के उल्टा बहता है।
Ise बनाइए और उलटाव साफ़ दिखता है: एक तरफ़ supply है, एक series resistor current को सीमित करता है, और दूसरी तरफ़ battery है जिसे उल्टा चलाया जा रहा है।

<curious>Ab sign पलटता है</curious>, और इसे रटने की जगह वजह कहना बेहतर है। External source को cell का अपना electromotive force और उसका अंदरूनी drop दोनों पार करने पड़ते हैं, इसलिए दोनों terms ज़रूरी terminal voltage में जुड़ते हैं।
Isse मिलता है terminal voltage equals E plus I r, और इसलिए charge होती battery का terminal voltage उसके electromotive force से ज़्यादा होता है।
Ab दोनों अनजान राशियाँ निकालने की प्रक्रिया। Cell को एक known resistance से जोड़िए और current मापिए, फिर एक अलग known resistance के साथ दोहराइए।
Har measurement आपको electromotive force देता है, current into loop की कुल resistance के रूप में, इसलिए आपके पास बिलकुल एक जैसी शक्ल के दो equations हैं।

Akela एक measurement दो अनजान राशियों में एक ही equation देता है और हल नहीं हो सकता। दूसरा स्वतंत्र measurement system को बंद कर देता है, और दोनों expressions को बराबर रखने पर electromotive force हट जाता है और internal resistance एक ही क़दम में निकल आती है।

sections.title: Worked example: current and terminal voltage of a loaded cell

board_events.text: Worked example, C B S E board level: a loaded cell
A cell of electromotive force twelve volt and internal resistance zero point five ohm is connected to an external resistance of five point five ohm.
Find the current in the circuit and the terminal voltage of the cell.
Cross-check the terminal voltage the other way: it must also equal the drop across the external resistor.
The terminal voltage sits below the electromotive force by exactly the internal drop of one volt, as a discharging cell requires.

segments.text: The first worked example is at C B S E board level and exercises both halves of the terminal voltage relation on one circuit.
A cell of electromotive force twelve volt and internal resistance zero point five ohm is connected to an external resistance of five point five ohm.
You are asked for the current in the circuit and for the terminal voltage of the cell.
For the current, remember the internal resistance is part of the loop. Add it to the external resistance to get a total of six ohm, and twelve volt across six ohm gives two amperes.
For the terminal voltage, subtract the internal drop. Two amperes through half an ohm loses one volt inside the cell, so eleven volt reaches the outside world.
<curious>Now use the free cross-check we set up.</curious> The terminal voltage must also equal the drop across the external resistor.
Two amperes through five point five ohm gives eleven volt, which agrees exactly with the first calculation.

Read the answer physically before moving on. The terminal voltage sits below the electromotive force by exactly the internal drop of one volt, which is what a discharging cell must do. If it had come out above twelve volt, something would be wrong.
Pehla worked example C B S E board level का है और एक ही circuit पर terminal voltage वाले relation के दोनों हिस्सों का अभ्यास कराता है।
Ek cell जिसका electromotive force बारह volt और internal resistance zero point पाँच ohm है, पाँच point पाँच ohm की external resistance से जुड़ा है।
Aapse circuit का current और cell का terminal voltage पूछा गया है।
<curious>Current के लिए याद रखिए कि internal resistance loop का हिस्सा है।</curious> उसे external resistance में जोड़िए तो कुल छह ohm मिलता है, और छह ohm पर बारह volt देता है दो ampere।
Terminal voltage के लिए अंदरूनी drop घटाइए। आधे ohm में से दो ampere गुज़रने पर cell के अंदर एक volt खो जाता है, इसलिए बाहर की दुनिया तक ग्यारह volt पहुँचता है।
Ab वो मुफ़्त cross-check इस्तेमाल कीजिए जो हमने बनाया था। Terminal voltage external resistor पर के drop के भी बराबर होना चाहिए।
Paanch point पाँच ohm में से दो ampere देता है ग्यारह volt, जो पहली गणना से बिलकुल मेल खाता है।

Aage बढ़ने से पहले answer को physically पढ़िए। Terminal voltage electromotive force से ठीक एक volt के अंदरूनी drop जितना नीचे है, और discharge होते cell को यही करना चाहिए। अगर बारह volt से ऊपर आता तो कुछ ग़लत होता।

sections.title: Worked example: internal resistance from two readings

board_events.text: Worked example, N E E T speed trap: internal resistance from readings
A cell reads one point five volt across its terminals on open circuit. Connected to a four ohm resistor, the terminal voltage falls to one point two volt.
The trap: trying to find the current from $E$ and $r$ before knowing $r$, which goes in circles.
The open-circuit reading is the electromotive force directly, because no current flows and there is no internal drop.
Get the current from the loaded terminal voltage and the external resistor. Both of those are given.
Memory hook: the voltage you lost, divided by the current you drew, is the internal resistance.

segments.text: The second worked example is a N E E T speed trap, and the trap is a reasoning loop rather than an arithmetic slip.
A cell reads one point five volt across its terminals on open circuit. When it is connected to a four ohm resistor, the terminal voltage falls to one point two volt. Find the internal resistance.

<chuckle>Here is where students get stuck.</chuckle> They try to find the current from the electromotive force and the internal resistance, but the internal resistance is exactly what they are trying to find. That reasoning goes in circles.
Break the loop by reading the data properly. The open-circuit reading is the electromotive force directly, because no current flows and so there is no internal drop at all.
Now get the current from the other side entirely. The loaded terminal voltage sits across the external resistor, so the current is one point two divided by four, which is zero point three amperes.
Notice what made that work. Both quantities in that division were given to you, so no unknown was involved.
With the current known, the lost voltage equals the internal drop. One point five minus one point two is zero point three volt, and dividing by zero point three amperes gives one ohm.
The memory hook is worth carrying: the voltage you lost, divided by the current you drew, is the internal resistance. Say it that way and the circular reasoning never starts.
Doosra worked example N E E T का speed trap है, और जाल arithmetic की चूक नहीं, सोच का एक चक्कर है।
Ek cell open circuit पर अपने terminals पर एक point पाँच volt पढ़ता है। चार ohm के resistor से जोड़ने पर terminal voltage गिरकर एक point दो volt हो जाता है। Internal resistance निकालिए।
Ye रही वो जगह जहाँ students अटक जाते हैं। वो electromotive force और internal resistance से current निकालने लगते हैं, लेकिन internal resistance तो वही है जो निकालनी है। वो सोच चक्कर में घूमती रहती है।
<curious>Chakkar तोड़िए data को ठीक से पढ़कर।</curious> Open-circuit की reading सीधे electromotive force है, क्योंकि कोई current बहता ही नहीं और इसलिए कोई अंदरूनी drop है ही नहीं।
Ab current पूरी तरह दूसरी तरफ़ से निकालिए। Loaded terminal voltage external resistor पर है, इसलिए current है एक point दो बटा चार, यानी zero point तीन ampere।
Dhyan दीजिए किस चीज़ ने ये काम कराया। उस भाग में दोनों राशियाँ आपको दी गई थीं, इसलिए कोई अनजान चीज़ शामिल ही नहीं हुई।
Current पता चलते ही, खोया हुआ voltage अंदरूनी drop के बराबर है। एक point पाँच minus एक point दो है zero point तीन volt, और zero point तीन ampere से divide करने पर एक ohm मिलता है।
Yaad रखने वाला हुक साथ ले जाइए: जो voltage खोया, उसे उस current से divide कीजिए जो खींचा, वही internal resistance है। इसे ऐसे कहिए और वो गोल गोल सोच शुरू ही नहीं होगी।

board_events.text: Check against the first equation: zero point five zero times twelve is six volt, which agrees.

segments.text: The third worked example is at J E E Main level and applies the two-load method we set up in the derivation.
Connected to a ten ohm resistor, a cell gives a current of zero point five zero ampere. Connected instead to a four ohm resistor, the same cell gives one point zero ampere.
You are asked for both the electromotive force and the internal resistance, neither of which is given.
Think about it graphically first. You have been handed two working points on the same straight line, and two points determine a line completely, which is why the problem is solvable at all.
Algebraically, write the electromotive force as current times total loop resistance for each case. That gives two expressions for the same electromotive force.

<curious>Now equate them.</curious> The electromotive force cancels out, leaving an equation in the internal resistance alone, and expanding gives five plus half r equals four plus r, so the internal resistance is two ohm.
Back-substitute into either equation. Using the second, one point zero times four plus two gives an electromotive force of six volt.

Always check against the equation you did not use for the back-substitution. Zero point five zero times ten plus two is zero point five zero times twelve, which is six volt. Both equations agree, so the pair is correct.
Teesra worked example J E E Main level का है और वो two-load method लगाता है जो हमने derivation में बनाया था।
Das ohm के resistor से जोड़ने पर एक cell zero point पाँच शून्य ampere current देता है। उसी cell को चार ohm से जोड़ने पर वो एक point शून्य ampere देता है।
Aapse electromotive force और internal resistance दोनों पूछी गई हैं, और दोनों में से कोई दी नहीं गई।
Pehle इसे graph की तरह सोचिए। आपको एक ही सीधी line पर दो working points दिए गए हैं, और दो points एक line को पूरी तरह तय कर देते हैं, इसीलिए ये problem हल हो पाती है।
Algebra में, हर मामले के लिए electromotive force को current into loop की कुल resistance लिखिए। इससे एक ही electromotive force के लिए दो expressions मिलती हैं।
Ab इन्हें बराबर रखिए। Electromotive force कट जाता है, और सिर्फ़ internal resistance वाला equation बचता है, जिसे खोलने पर मिलता है पाँच plus आधा r बराबर चार plus r, यानी internal resistance दो ohm।
<curious>Kisi भी एक equation में वापस रखिए।</curious> दूसरे से, एक point शून्य into चार plus दो देता है electromotive force छह volt।

Hamesha उस equation से जाँचिए जो back-substitution में इस्तेमाल नहीं की। Zero point पाँच शून्य into दस plus दो यानी zero point पाँच शून्य into बारह, जो छह volt है। दोनों equations मिल रहे हैं, इसलिए जोड़ी सही है।

board_events.caption: The supply drives current backwards into the battery through the series resistor, against the battery's own electromotive force.

board_events.text: The supply must overcome the battery's back electromotive force, so only the difference drives the current.
Cross-check: power into the battery is $VI = 10.88$ watt, internal heating is $I^2r = 1.28$ watt, and the difference is exactly the stored power.

segments.text: The final worked example for this subtopic is at J E E Advanced level and uses the charging sign, which is where most students lose the marks.
A battery of electromotive force six volt and internal resistance zero point five ohm is being charged by a ten volt supply through a series resistor of two ohm.
Draw it before calculating. The supply is driving current backwards into the battery, against the battery's own electromotive force, and the series resistor limits how much.
That gives the key insight for part one. The supply must overcome the battery's back electromotive force, so only the difference between the two voltages is available to drive current.
The net driving voltage is ten minus six, which is four volt, across a total series resistance of two plus zero point five. That gives one point six amperes.

For part two, use the charging sign. The terminal voltage is the electromotive force plus the internal drop, giving six point eight volt, which is above the electromotive force exactly as a charging battery requires.
For part three, of the power delivered into the battery, the part stored as chemical energy is the electromotive force times the current, which is nine point six watt.

<curious>Cross-check the energy bookkeeping.</curious> Power into the battery is V I, ten point eight eight watt. Internal heating is I squared r, one point two eight watt. The difference is nine point six watt, exactly the stored power.
Is subtopic का आख़िरी worked example J E E Advanced level का है और charging वाला sign इस्तेमाल करता है, जहाँ ज़्यादातर students marks गँवाते हैं।
Ek battery जिसका electromotive force छह volt और internal resistance zero point पाँच ohm है, उसे दस volt की supply दो ohm के series resistor के ज़रिए charge कर रही है।
Calculate करने से पहले बनाइए। Supply battery में current उल्टा धकेल रही है, battery के अपने electromotive force के ख़िलाफ़, और series resistor तय कर रहा है कि कितना।
<curious>Isse पहले हिस्से की मुख्य समझ मिलती है।</curious> Supply को battery का back electromotive force पार करना है, इसलिए current चलाने के लिए सिर्फ़ दोनों voltages का फ़र्क़ ही उपलब्ध है।
Net driving voltage है दस minus छह, यानी चार volt, कुल दो plus zero point पाँच की series resistance पर। इससे मिलता है एक point छह ampere।

Doosre हिस्से के लिए charging वाला sign लगाइए। Terminal voltage है electromotive force plus अंदरूनी drop, यानी छह point आठ volt, जो electromotive force से ऊपर है, बिलकुल जैसा charge होती battery के लिए ज़रूरी है।
Teesre हिस्से के लिए, battery में जाती power में से जो हिस्सा chemical energy बनकर जमा होता है वो है electromotive force into current, यानी नौ point छह watt।

Energy का हिसाब cross-check कीजिए। Battery में जाती कुल power है V I, छह point आठ into एक point छह, यानी दस point आठ आठ watt। अंदरूनी heating है I squared r, एक point दो आठ watt। फ़र्क़ है नौ point छह watt, ठीक वही जमा हुई power।

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips for EMF and internal resistance

board_events.text: Pitfalls that cost marks, and the pro-tips that save time
Confusing electromotive force with terminal voltage. The first is fixed; the second depends on the current drawn.
They are equal only on open circuit, which is exactly why an open-circuit voltmeter reading is the electromotive force.
Using the discharge sign for a charging battery. That gives a terminal voltage below the electromotive force, which is impossible while charging.
Thinking the short-circuit current is infinite. It is $E/r$, large but strictly finite.
Calling electromotive force a force. It is energy per unit charge, measured in volt.
For two-load problems, write $E = I(R + r)$ for each case and equate. The electromotive force cancels and $r$ falls out in one step.

segments.text: Let us close this subtopic with the four errors that reliably cost marks and the two shortcuts that reliably save time.
The first is confusing electromotive force with terminal voltage. The electromotive force is a fixed property of the cell; the terminal voltage depends on how much current you are drawing.
They are equal only on open circuit, which is exactly why an open-circuit voltmeter reading gives you the electromotive force, and why a loaded reading does not.
The second is using the discharge sign for a battery that is being charged. That hands you a terminal voltage below the electromotive force, which is physically impossible while charging.
So build the habit of asking which way the current is flowing before you choose the sign, and sanity check the answer against the direction afterwards.
The third is thinking the short-circuit current is infinite. It is the electromotive force over the internal resistance, large but strictly finite, and the internal resistance is what caps it.
The fourth is calling electromotive force a force. It is energy per unit charge, measured in volt, and boards give away a mark for saying so correctly.

<excited>Now the shortcuts.</excited> The cleanest route to the internal resistance from data is the lost voltage over the current drawn. And for two-load problems, write E equals I times R plus r for each case and equate, because the electromotive force cancels and r falls out in a single step.
Is subtopic को उन चार ग़लतियों के साथ ख़त्म करते हैं जो पक्के तौर पर marks काटती हैं, और उन दो shortcuts के साथ जो पक्के तौर पर time बचाते हैं।
Pehli है electromotive force और terminal voltage को मिला देना। Electromotive force cell की तय property है; terminal voltage इस पर निर्भर है कि आप कितना current खींच रहे हैं।
<curious>Ye सिर्फ़ open circuit पर बराबर होते हैं</curious>, और ठीक इसीलिए open-circuit voltmeter की reading आपको electromotive force देती है, और loaded reading नहीं देती।
Doosri है charge होती battery के लिए discharge वाला sign लगाना। इससे terminal voltage electromotive force से नीचे आ जाता है, जो charging के दौरान physically नामुमकिन है।
To sign चुनने से पहले ये पूछने की आदत बनाइए कि current किस तरफ़ बह रहा है, और बाद में answer को दिशा से मिलाकर जाँचिए।
Teesri है ये समझना कि short-circuit current infinite होता है। वो electromotive force over internal resistance है, बड़ा लेकिन बिलकुल finite, और internal resistance ही उसे बाँधती है।
Chauthi है electromotive force को force कह देना। ये energy per unit charge है, volt में मापी जाती है, और boards इसे सही कहने पर एक mark दे देते हैं।

Ab shortcuts। Data से internal resistance तक का सबसे साफ़ रास्ता है खोया हुआ voltage बटा खींचा गया current। और two-load problems में हर मामले के लिए E equals I into R plus r लिखकर बराबर रखिए, क्योंकि electromotive force कट जाता है और r एक ही क़दम में निकल आती है।

sections.title: Why we combine cells at all

board_events.text: Why we combine cells at all
One cell can only push so hard and supply so much. Combining cells decides whether we gain voltage or current capacity.
Cells in series are stacked head to tail, like several people lifting a load to successive shelves. Each adds its own lift.
So the electromotive forces add, but each cell also brings its own internal resistance into the line, so those add too.
Cells in parallel sit side by side, all positive terminals joined and all negative terminals joined, sharing the same lifting job.
The voltage stays at one cell's worth, but the internal resistances combine in parallel and drop.
Series is like joining batteries end to end in a torch for a brighter beam. Parallel is like wiring two car batteries to crank a heavy engine.
Series multiplies the push; parallel multiplies the stamina.

segments.text: Having made the single cell realistic, we now ask what happens when you have several of them and a choice about how to wire them.
One cell can only push so hard and supply so much. To get more we combine cells, and how we combine them decides whether we gain voltage or current capacity.
Cells in series are stacked head to tail, like several people lifting a load to successive shelves. Each person adds their own lift to the one before.
So in series the electromotive forces add up. But notice the cost: each cell also brings its own internal resistance into the line, so those add as well.
Cells in parallel sit side by side instead, with all the positive terminals joined and all the negative terminals joined, like several people sharing the same lifting job.

<curious>Now the voltage does not add at all.</curious> It stays at one cell's worth, because every cell spans the same pair of nodes. What changes is that the internal resistances combine in parallel and drop.
The everyday pictures are worth carrying. Series is joining batteries end to end in a torch to get a brighter beam. Parallel is wiring two identical car batteries together to crank a heavy engine.
Compress it to one line: series multiplies the push, and parallel multiplies the stamina. Which one you want depends entirely on the load, and that is the next thing we pin down.
Ek cell को हक़ीक़त के क़रीब लाने के बाद, अब हम पूछते हैं कि क्या हो जब आपके पास कई cells हों और उन्हें जोड़ने का विकल्प भी।
Ek cell उतना ही धक्का और उतना ही current दे सकता है। ज़्यादा के लिए हम cells जोड़ते हैं, और जोड़ने का तरीक़ा तय करता है कि हमें voltage मिलेगा या current capacity।
<curious>Series में cells सिर से पूँछ तक जुड़े होते हैं</curious>, जैसे कई लोग एक बोझ को एक के बाद एक shelf तक उठाते हैं। हर व्यक्ति पिछले वाले पर अपना lift जोड़ता है।
To series में electromotive forces जुड़ जाते हैं। लेकिन क़ीमत भी देखिए: हर cell अपनी internal resistance भी line में ले आता है, इसलिए वो भी जुड़ती हैं।
Parallel में cells इसकी जगह साथ साथ बैठते हैं, सारे positive terminals जुड़े और सारे negative जुड़े, जैसे कई लोग एक ही उठाने का काम मिलकर कर रहे हों।
Ab voltage बिलकुल नहीं जुड़ता। वो एक cell जितना ही रहता है, क्योंकि हर cell उन्हीं दो nodes के बीच है। जो बदलता है वो ये कि internal resistances parallel में जुड़कर गिर जाती हैं।
Roz की तस्वीरें साथ ले जाइए। Series है torch में batteries को end to end जोड़ना ताकि beam तेज़ हो। Parallel है दो एक जैसी car batteries जोड़ना ताकि भारी engine crank हो सके।
Ise एक line में समेटिए: series धक्का बढ़ाता है, और parallel दमखम। आपको कौन सा चाहिए ये पूरी तरह load पर है, और अगली बात हम यही तय करते हैं।

sections.title: Matching the grouping to the load

board_events.text: Matching the grouping to the load
Series grouping is what you want when the external resistance is large.
You need a big push, and the modest extra internal resistance hardly matters beside a large external resistance.
Parallel grouping is what you want when the external resistance is small.
You need to supply a large current, and cutting the internal resistance is what stops it being choked.
For the best of both, mixed grouping uses rows of cells in series, with several such rows placed in parallel.

board_events.text: By choosing how many cells go in each row and how many rows, you tune the combination to deliver maximum current into a given load.

segments.text: The choice between series and parallel is not a matter of taste. It is decided entirely by the size of the external resistance.
Series grouping is what you want when the external resistance is large.
The reasoning is straightforward. You need a big push to drive current through a large resistance, and the modest extra internal resistance you have added hardly matters beside it.
Parallel grouping is what you want when the external resistance is small.
Here the constraint is different. With a small load you need to supply a large current, and cutting the internal resistance is exactly what stops that current being choked before it reaches the load.
<curious>For the best of both, we use mixed grouping.</curious> Rows of cells in series, with several such rows placed in parallel between the same two bus bars.
Picture it as a rectangular array. Each row contributes voltage by stacking cells, and the rows in parallel bring the combined internal resistance back down.

By choosing how many cells go in each row and how many rows you use, you can tune the combination to deliver maximum current into a given load. That optimisation is the mathematical heart of this subtopic.
Series और parallel के बीच का चुनाव पसंद का मामला नहीं है। ये पूरी तरह external resistance के आकार से तय होता है।
Series grouping तब चाहिए जब external resistance बड़ी हो।
Vajah सीधी है। बड़ी resistance में current चलाने के लिए बड़ा धक्का चाहिए, और आपने जो थोड़ी सी अतिरिक्त internal resistance जोड़ी है वो उसके सामने ज़्यादा मायने नहीं रखती।
Parallel grouping तब चाहिए जब external resistance छोटी हो।
<curious>Yahan बाधा अलग है।</curious> छोटे load के साथ आपको बड़ा current देना है, और internal resistance घटाना ही वो चीज़ है जो उस current को load तक पहुँचने से पहले गला घुटने से बचाती है।
Dono का फ़ायदा लेने के लिए हम mixed grouping इस्तेमाल करते हैं। Series में cells की rows, और ऐसी कई rows उन्हीं दो bus bars के बीच parallel में।
Ise एक आयताकार array की तरह देखिए। हर row cells जोड़कर voltage देती है, और parallel में लगी rows मिलकर internal resistance वापस नीचे ले आती हैं।
Har row में कितने cells और कितनी rows, ये चुनकर आप combination को इस तरह tune कर सकते हैं कि दिए गए load में सबसे ज़्यादा current जाए। वही optimisation इस subtopic का गणितीय दिल है।

sections.title: The assumptions behind the clean rules

board_events.text: The assumptions behind the clean rules
The rule that electromotive forces add in series assumes all cells point the same way.
If one cell is reversed, its electromotive force subtracts instead. And it changes the total by twice its value, not once.
A reversed cell goes from contributing plus $E$ to contributing minus $E$, so the swing is $2E$.
The simple parallel result $r_{eq} = r/n$ assumes the cells are identical. Unequal cells need the general weighted formula.
Throughout, we treat each cell as an ideal electromotive force in series with a constant internal resistance, in the steady state.
Real internal resistance drifts with temperature and state of charge, so these results are a model rather than an exact description.

segments.text: Before the formulas, three assumptions are worth stating, because two of them generate exam questions in their own right.
The first is that the rule about electromotive forces adding in series assumes all the cells point the same way, aiding one another.
If one cell is reversed, its electromotive force subtracts instead. And here is the detail students miss: it changes the total by twice its value, not once.
Write it generally. For k reversed cells out of n identical ones, the net electromotive force is n minus two k, times E.
<curious>The factor of two is the whole point.</curious> A reversed cell goes from contributing plus E to contributing minus E, so the swing between those two states is two E, not E.

The second assumption sits in the parallel result. The clean form, internal resistance over n, assumes the cells are identical. Unequal cells need the general weighted formula, which we meet in the next section.
The third is the one we have carried all along. We treat each cell as an ideal electromotive force in series with a constant internal resistance, in the steady state.

Real internal resistance drifts with temperature and with state of charge, so everything that follows is a model rather than an exact description. That is worth a sentence in any answer that asks for limitations.
Formulas से पहले तीन assumptions कहने लायक़ हैं, क्योंकि उनमें से दो अपने आप में exam के सवाल पैदा करती हैं।
Pehli ये कि series में electromotive forces जुड़ने वाला नियम मानकर चलता है कि सारे cells एक ही तरफ़ मुड़े हैं, एक दूसरे का साथ देते हुए।
<curious>Agar एक cell उल्टा लगा हो तो उसका electromotive force घटता है।</curious> और ये रही वो बारीकी जो students चूक जाते हैं: वो कुल को अपनी value का दोगुना बदलता है, इकहरा नहीं।
Ise आम तौर पर लिखिए। n barabar cells में से k उल्टे हों, तो net electromotive force है n minus two k, into E।
Do का वो factor ही पूरी बात है। उल्टा cell plus E देने से minus E देने पर चला जाता है, इसलिए उन दो हालतों के बीच का झूला दो E है, E नहीं।
Doosri assumption parallel वाले नतीजे में है। साफ़ रूप, internal resistance over n, मानता है कि cells barabar हैं। अलग अलग cells के लिए general weighted formula चाहिए, जो अगले section में मिलेगा।
Teesri वही है जो हम शुरू से साथ लिए चल रहे हैं। हम हर cell को एक ideal electromotive force मानते हैं जो स्थिर internal resistance के series में है, steady state में।

Asli internal resistance temperature और cell कितना भरा है इससे खिसकती है, इसलिए आगे जो कुछ आता है वो एक model है, ठीक ठीक वर्णन नहीं। Limitations पूछने वाले किसी भी answer में ये एक वाक्य के क़ाबिल है।

sections.title: Series and parallel combination formulas

board_events.text: Series and parallel combination formulas

board_events.latex: E_{eq} = \sum E_i, \qquad r_{eq} = \sum r_i, \qquad I = \frac{E_{eq}}{R + r_{eq}}

board_events.text: In series both the electromotive forces and the internal resistances add.

board_events.latex: \text{n identical: } E_{eq} = nE, \quad r_{eq} = nr, \quad I = \frac{nE}{R + nr}

board_events.text: If $k$ of the $n$ identical cells are reversed, replace the numerator electromotive force by $(n - 2k)E$.

board_events.latex: \text{n identical in parallel: } E_{eq} = E, \quad r_{eq} = \frac{r}{n}, \quad I = \frac{nE}{nR + r}

board_events.text: The electromotive force is unchanged in parallel. Only the internal resistance falls, by a factor of $n$.
Symbols throughout: $E$ electromotive force in volt, $r$ internal resistance in ohm, $R$ external load in ohm, $I$ current in ampere.

segments.text: Here are the two basic combination results, together with the reversed-cell correction that examiners like to slip in.
In general, cells in series add their electromotive forces and add their internal resistances, and the current follows from the same single-cell relation as before.
Say both halves out loud when you learn this, because students reliably remember that the voltages add and forget that the internal resistances add too.
For n identical cells in series, that specialises to n E and n r, giving a current of n E over R plus n r.

<whisper>And here is the correction.</whisper> If k of those n identical cells are reversed, replace the numerator electromotive force by n minus two k, times E, while the internal resistance stays at n r because resistance does not care about polarity.
For n identical cells in parallel, the electromotive force stays at E while the internal resistance falls to r over n, giving the current shown.
The contrast is the thing to hold. In parallel the electromotive force is completely unchanged. Only the internal resistance falls, and it falls by a factor of n.
For the symbols throughout this subtopic: E is electromotive force in volt, r is internal resistance in ohm, R is the external load in ohm, and I is current in ampere.
<curious>Ye रहे दो बुनियादी combination के नतीजे</curious>, साथ में उल्टे cell वाला सुधार जिसे examiners चुपके से डालना पसंद करते हैं।
Aam तौर पर, series के cells अपने electromotive forces जोड़ते हैं और अपनी internal resistances भी, और current पहले वाले उसी single-cell relation से निकलता है।
Ise सीखते समय दोनों हिस्से ज़ोर से बोलिए, क्योंकि students पक्के तौर पर याद रखते हैं कि voltages जुड़ते हैं और भूल जाते हैं कि internal resistances भी जुड़ती हैं।
n barabar cells series में हों तो ये बनता है n E और n r, और current मिलता है n E over R plus n r।

Aur ये रहा सुधार। उन n barabar cells में से k उल्टे हों, तो numerator के electromotive force की जगह n minus two k, into E रखिए, जबकि internal resistance n r ही रहती है क्योंकि resistance को polarity की परवाह नहीं।
n barabar cells parallel में हों तो electromotive force E ही रहता है जबकि internal resistance गिरकर r over n हो जाती है, और current वैसा मिलता है जैसा दिखाया है।
Farq को पकड़िए। Parallel में electromotive force बिलकुल नहीं बदलता। सिर्फ़ internal resistance गिरती है, और n के factor से गिरती है।
Is पूरे subtopic के चिह्न: E है electromotive force volt में, r है internal resistance ohm में, R है external load ohm में, और I है current ampere में।

sections.title: Unequal cells in parallel, and mixed grouping

board_events.text: Unequal cells in parallel, and mixed grouping
The equivalent electromotive force is a weighted average, pulled towards whichever cell has the lower internal resistance.

board_events.latex: \text{Mixed, m rows of n: } E_{eq} = nE, \qquad r_{eq} = \frac{nr}{m}

board_events.text: In words: arrange the cells so that the combination's own internal resistance equals the external resistance.

segments.text: The second formula block handles the two cases that generate the harder questions: unequal cells, and mixed grouping.
For two different cells in parallel, the equivalent electromotive force is not a simple average. It is the weighted form shown, and the second version makes the weighting explicit.
The equivalent internal resistance is just the ordinary parallel combination of the two internal resistances, which is the familiar product over sum.

<curious>Read the weighting physically.</curious> The equivalent electromotive force is pulled towards whichever cell has the lower internal resistance, because that cell has more say in what the pair does.

For mixed grouping, with m rows of n cells each, the equivalent electromotive force is n E because each row stacks n cells, and the equivalent internal resistance is n r over m because m such rows sit in parallel.
Substituting into the single-cell current relation gives m n E over m R plus n r, which is the general mixed-grouping result.
That current is maximised when the external resistance equals n r over m, and at that point the maximum current is n E over two R.
State the condition in words, because that is how you will actually use it. Arrange the cells so that the combination's own internal resistance equals the external resistance.
Doosra formula हिस्सा उन दो मामलों को सँभालता है जो मुश्किल सवाल पैदा करते हैं: अलग अलग cells, और mixed grouping।
Parallel में दो अलग cells के लिए equivalent electromotive force कोई साधारण average नहीं है। ये दिखाया गया weighted रूप है, और दूसरा version उस weighting को साफ़ कर देता है।
Equivalent internal resistance बस दोनों internal resistances का साधारण parallel combination है, यानी वही जाना पहचाना product over sum।
Weighting को physically पढ़िए। Equivalent electromotive force उस cell की तरफ़ खिंचता है जिसकी internal resistance कम है, क्योंकि उस cell की जोड़ी पर ज़्यादा चलती है।

<curious>Mixed grouping के लिए</curious>, m rows और हर row में n cells, equivalent electromotive force n E है क्योंकि हर row n cells जोड़ती है, और equivalent internal resistance n r over m है क्योंकि ऐसी m rows parallel में बैठी हैं।
Ise single-cell वाले current relation में रखने पर मिलता है m n E over m R plus n r, जो mixed-grouping का आम नतीजा है।
Wo current तब सबसे ज़्यादा होता है जब external resistance n r over m के बराबर हो, और उस point पर maximum current है n E over two R।
Shart को शब्दों में कहिए, क्योंकि आप इसे असल में ऐसे ही इस्तेमाल करेंगे। Cells को इस तरह सजाइए कि combination की अपनी internal resistance external resistance के बराबर हो जाए।

segments.text: These two derivations are short, and doing them together makes the contrast between the groupings unmistakable.
For series, take n identical cells, each of electromotive force E and internal resistance r, connected head to tail across an external resistance R.
Draw them in a single row. There is exactly one loop, and the same current flows through every cell and through the external resistor in turn.
Applying the loop rule around that single loop gives n E equals the current times R plus n r, so the current is n E over R plus n r.
Say why each factor appears. Going around the loop, every cell contributes plus E to the driving electromotive force because they all aid, and every cell contributes r to the resistance in the path.
<curious>Now change the wiring completely.</curious> Take the same n cells with all the positives joined and all the negatives joined, across the same external resistance.
Each cell now spans the same pair of nodes, so the combined electromotive force is just E and does not add. But the n internal resistances sit in parallel, giving r over n.
Substituting gives a current of n E over n R plus r. Compare the two results: series wins when R is large, and parallel wins when R is small, exactly as the intuition predicted.
Ye दोनों derivations छोटी हैं, और इन्हें साथ करने से groupings का फ़र्क़ बिलकुल साफ़ हो जाता है।
Series के लिए n barabar cells लीजिए, हर एक का electromotive force E और internal resistance r, जो external resistance R के आर पार सिर से पूँछ तक जुड़े हैं।
Inhe एक ही row में बनाइए। ठीक एक loop है, और वही current हर cell से और बारी बारी external resistor से बहता है।
Us एक loop पर loop rule लगाने से मिलता है n E बराबर current into R plus n r, इसलिए current है n E over R plus n r।
<curious>Har factor क्यों आया, ये कहिए।</curious> Loop में चलते हुए हर cell driving electromotive force में plus E देता है क्योंकि सब साथ दे रहे हैं, और हर cell रास्ते की resistance में r देता है।
Ab wiring पूरी तरह बदल दीजिए। वही n cells लीजिए जिनके सारे positive जुड़े हैं और सारे negative जुड़े हैं, उसी external resistance के आर पार।
Ab हर cell उन्हीं दो nodes के बीच है, इसलिए मिला हुआ electromotive force सिर्फ़ E है और जुड़ता नहीं। लेकिन n internal resistances parallel में बैठती हैं, जिससे मिलता है r over n।
Rakh कर देखिए तो current निकलता है n E over n R plus r। दोनों नतीजे मिलाइए: R बड़ी हो तो series जीतता है, और R छोटी हो तो parallel, ठीक जैसा intuition ने बताया था।

sections.title: Derivation: the mixed-grouping optimisation

board_events.text: Derivation: the mixed-grouping optimisation
Take $m$ rows in parallel, each row containing $n$ identical cells in series, feeding an external resistance $R$.
With the total number of cells $N = mn$ fixed, the numerator is fixed, so the current is largest when the denominator is smallest.
The product of the two denominator terms is a constant, so only their sum can vary. That is exactly the setup for the A M G M inequality.
For a fixed product, a sum of two positive terms is smallest when the two terms are equal.

segments.text: This is the elegant one, and the logic is worth following rather than memorising, because the same trick appears elsewhere in physics.
Take m rows in parallel, each row containing n identical cells in series, feeding an external resistance R.
Each row has electromotive force n E and resistance n r, and m such rows in parallel give n r over m, so the current is m n E over m R plus n r.
Now fix the total number of cells at N equals m n, since a real problem gives you a fixed number to arrange. That fixes the numerator, so the current is largest when the denominator is smallest.
<curious>Now look at the two denominator terms.</curious> Their product is m R times n r, which is m n R r, which is N R r. Every factor in that is fixed, so the product is a constant.
A sum of two positive terms whose product is constant is exactly the setup for the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality.
For a fixed product, the sum of two positive terms is smallest when the two terms are equal.
Setting m R equal to n r is therefore the condition, and rearranging shows it means the external resistance equals the equivalent internal resistance.

Substituting back gives a maximum current of n E over two R, and notice this is the same matching idea we met in maximum power transfer, now reached by choosing an arrangement rather than turning a dial.
Ye वाली सुंदर है, और इसका जवाब रटने की जगह तर्क का पीछा करना बेहतर है, क्योंकि यही तरकीब physics में और जगह भी आती है।
<curious>m rows parallel में लीजिए</curious>, हर row में n barabar cells series में, जो external resistance R को चला रही हैं।
Har row का electromotive force n E और resistance n r है, और ऐसी m rows parallel में equivalent internal resistance n r over m देती हैं, इसलिए current है m n E over m R plus n r।

Ab cells की कुल संख्या N बराबर m n तय कर दीजिए, क्योंकि असली problem में आपके पास सजाने को तय संख्या में cells होते हैं। इससे numerator तय हो जाता है, इसलिए current ठीक तब सबसे बड़ा होगा जब denominator सबसे छोटा हो।
Ab denominator के दोनों terms देखिए। उनका गुणा है m R into n r, यानी m n R r, यानी N R r। उसमें हर factor तय है, इसलिए गुणा एक constant है।
Do धनात्मक terms का जोड़ जिनका गुणा constant हो, ये बिलकुल वही हालत है जिसके लिए arithmetic-geometric mean inequality बनी है, और वो inequality बताती है कि जोड़ कब सबसे नीचे जाता है।
Tay गुणा के लिए, दो धनात्मक terms का जोड़ तब सबसे छोटा होता है जब दोनों terms barabar हों।
Isliye m R को n r के बराबर रखना ही शर्त है, और rearrange करने पर दिखता है कि इसका मतलब है external resistance बराबर equivalent internal resistance।
Wapas रखने पर maximum current मिलता है n E over two R, और ध्यान दीजिए ये वही matching वाला विचार है जो maximum power transfer में मिला था, अब dial घुमाकर नहीं बल्कि arrangement चुनकर हासिल किया गया।

sections.title: Worked example: three cells in series

board_events.text: Worked example, C B S E board level: three cells in series
Three identical cells, each of electromotive force two volt and internal resistance zero point five ohm, are connected in series.
They drive an external resistance of four point five ohm. Find the current in the circuit.
Reduce the grouping to a single equivalent cell before touching the load. That habit handles every problem in this subtopic.
Both the electromotive forces and the internal resistances tripled, because all three cells sit in the same single loop.
Check the scale: three cells of two volt cannot produce more than six volt, and the current is comfortably below the short-circuit value.

segments.text: The first worked example for this subtopic is at C B S E board level, and it is the cleanest possible use of the series result.
Three identical cells, each of electromotive force two volt and internal resistance zero point five ohm, are connected in series.
They drive an external resistance of four point five ohm, and you are asked for the current in the circuit.

<whisper>Build the habit here.</whisper> Reduce the grouping to a single equivalent cell before you touch the load. That one habit handles every problem in this subtopic, however the cells are arranged.
In series both quantities triple. The equivalent electromotive force is six volt, and the equivalent internal resistance is one point five ohm.
Now treat it as a single cell driving a load. Six volt across a total of four point five plus one point five, which is six ohm, gives exactly one ampere.
Notice that both quantities tripled, and say why. All three cells sit in the same single loop, so all three electromotive forces aid and all three internal resistances lie in the current path.

Finish by checking the scale. Three cells of two volt cannot possibly produce more than six volt, and one ampere is comfortably below the short-circuit value of six over one point five, which is four amperes.
Is subtopic का पहला worked example C B S E board level का है, और ये series वाले नतीजे का सबसे साफ़ इस्तेमाल है।
Teen barabar cells, हर एक का electromotive force दो volt और internal resistance zero point पाँच ohm, series में जुड़े हैं।
Wo चार point पाँच ohm की external resistance चला रहे हैं, और आपसे circuit का current पूछा गया है।
Yahan आदत बनाइए। Load को छूने से पहले grouping को एक equivalent cell में समेटिए। वही एक आदत इस subtopic की हर problem सँभाल लेती है, cells चाहे कैसे भी सजे हों।
<curious>Series में दोनों राशियाँ तिगुनी हो जाती हैं।</curious> Equivalent electromotive force है छह volt, और equivalent internal resistance एक point पाँच ohm।
Ab इसे एक अकेले cell की तरह मानिए जो load चला रहा है। कुल चार point पाँच plus एक point पाँच, यानी छह ohm पर छह volt देता है ठीक एक ampere।
Dhyan दीजिए कि दोनों राशियाँ तिगुनी हुईं, और वजह कहिए। तीनों cells उसी एक loop में हैं, इसलिए तीनों electromotive forces साथ देते हैं और तीनों internal resistances current के रास्ते में पड़ती हैं।
Pैमाने की जाँच से ख़त्म कीजिए। दो volt के तीन cells छह volt से ज़्यादा बना ही नहीं सकते, और एक ampere short-circuit की value छह बटा एक point पाँच यानी चार ampere से आराम से नीचे है।

sections.title: Worked example: four cells in parallel

board_events.text: Worked example, N E E T speed trap: cells in parallel
Four identical cells, each one point five volt with internal resistance one ohm, are connected in parallel across a two ohm resistor.
The trap: adding the electromotive forces to get six volt. Electromotive forces do not add in parallel.
Every cell spans the same pair of nodes, so they all sit at the same potential difference. Stacking is a series move.
Memory hook: parallel keeps the voltage and shrinks the internal resistance. Adding voltages is what series does.
Sanity check: the answer must be below the value a single cell would give into the same load, which is one point five over three.

segments.text: The second worked example is a N E E T speed trap, and it catches students who have learned the series rule and applied it everywhere.
Four identical cells, each one point five volt with internal resistance one ohm, are connected in parallel across a two ohm resistor. Find the current through the resistor.
<chuckle>Here is the trap.</chuckle> Students multiply four by one point five and write six volt. But electromotive forces do not add in parallel at all.
Understand why rather than memorising it. Every cell spans the same pair of nodes, so they all sit at the same potential difference, and stacking voltages is a series move.
So the equivalent electromotive force stays at one point five volt, unchanged. What does change is the internal resistance, which falls to r over n, a quarter of an ohm.
Now treat it as a single cell. One point five volt across two plus zero point two five, which is two point two five ohm, gives about zero point six seven amperes.
The memory hook is worth repeating: parallel keeps the voltage and shrinks the internal resistance. Adding voltages is what series does.

And here is a sanity check that catches the trap instantly. A single cell alone into the same load would give one point five over three, which is half an ampere. Four in parallel must give a bit more than that, and zero point six seven does. Six volt would have given nearly three amperes, which is absurd.
Doosra worked example N E E T का speed trap है, और ये उन students को पकड़ता है जिन्होंने series का नियम सीखकर उसे हर जगह लगा दिया।
Chaar barabar cells, हर एक एक point पाँच volt और internal resistance एक ohm, दो ohm के resistor के आर पार parallel में जुड़े हैं। Resistor से गुज़रता current निकालिए।
Ye रहा trap। Students चार को एक point पाँच से गुणा करके छह volt लिख देते हैं। लेकिन parallel में electromotive forces जुड़ते ही नहीं।
<curious>Ise रटने की जगह समझिए।</curious> हर cell उन्हीं दो nodes के बीच है, इसलिए सब एक ही potential difference पर बैठे हैं, और voltage जोड़ना series का काम है।
To equivalent electromotive force एक point पाँच volt ही रहता है, बिना बदले। जो बदलता है वो internal resistance है, जो गिरकर r over n यानी चौथाई ohm हो जाती है।
Ab इसे एक अकेले cell की तरह मानिए। दो plus zero point दो पाँच, यानी दो point दो पाँच ohm पर एक point पाँच volt देता है लगभग zero point छह सात ampere।
Yaad रखने वाला हुक दोहराने लायक़ है: parallel voltage वही रखता है और internal resistance घटाता है। Voltage जोड़ना series का काम है।

Aur ये रही वो जाँच जो trap को तुरंत पकड़ लेती है। अकेला एक cell उसी load में एक point पाँच बटा तीन यानी आधा ampere देता। Parallel में चार को उससे थोड़ा ज़्यादा देना चाहिए, और zero point छह सात देता है। छह volt होता तो लगभग तीन ampere आता, जो बेतुका है।

board_events.text: The equivalent electromotive force lands between the two cell values, and exactly midway here because the internal resistances are equal.
